note: Best measured policy-system configuration per benchmark and agent model (2026-11-04). Code lives on LOCAL branches of ~/dev/cuga-agent-gate (never push); runs use a snapshot of that branch's src/ as CUGA_SRC / --snapshot. Numbers are from changes.md; held-out sets are named. Snapshot branches were committed with hooks off so the code is byte-identical to the snapshot. Each entry names its profile file in benchmarks/policy_eval/profiles/ (key profile). Entries with "best": false are named profiles, not measured bests. Run a profile with harness/run.py. In an entry, runner, recipe, switches and env_file are the record of what was measured: those scripts and env files are in launchers/archive/ and run only from the local tag policy/pre-migration-removal (ENVIRONMENT.md).

profiles.name: B4T-F
profiles.recipe: automationbench/run_policy_types.sh <snapshot> <trial> with SUBSET=policy_types_holdout.json ONLY="A-F B4T-F" (cell B4T-F)
profiles.result: held-out policy_types_holdout.json (35 tasks, 2 trials): partial 42.7% vs CUGA alone 23.8% (+18.9, 24/6 tasks, p=0.001); AA 31.8% vs 12.9%; runs breaking a guardrail 19/64 vs 24/64

profiles.name: A-F (CUGA alone)
profiles.result: policy_types_holdout2 (pg, 2 trials): 80.9% partial, 53.2% strict, 1 guardrail broken in 60 runs; B4T-F was worse (75.1%, -5.8 paired, 8 better / 13 worse, p = 0.383, 24 broken)
profiles.why_no_policy: control by agent strength: the policy layer's control hurts a strong agent here

profiles.name: T (SOP tracker v3)
profiles.result: test split 40 tasks x 2 runs: 63.8% -> 76.2% (per task 9 better / 3 worse, p=0.146); test split was seen before the freeze

profiles.name: L (SOP loop control mode + procedure guide), round 1
profiles.recipe: CUGA_SRC=<snapshot>/src CUGA_ENV_FILE=cuga.fc.dsv4.env SOP_LOOP=1 HOOKS_MODULE=$PWD/handbook/guide_hooks.py:make_hooks python -I handbook/run_cuga_handbook.py --tasks all --run <run> --arm L --trial <n> -j 3
profiles.result: 3 public tasks, round 1 (hbb, 3 trials): 117/153 (76.5%) vs alone 86/153 (56.2%); pooled 3 rounds 73.4% vs 59.3%; in-sample only

profiles.name: L (SOP loop control mode + procedure guide with evidence)
profiles.result: trial 5 only: 23/51 vs alone 20/51 (discovery 19/51); weak evidence

profiles.name: GW (procedure graph as policy tools + must-not gate at write time)
profiles.graphs: policy_eval/graphs_handbook/claude_v1/<task>.json (hand-built by Claude from each SOP; *_graph.py rebuild them)
profiles.recipe: handbook/run_store_task.sh <snapshot of the gate branch> <task> <run prefix> 1 2 3 (runs A and GW at the same time; needs the Gemini LiteLLM key)
profiles.result: 3 public tasks, latest version, same time: CUGA alone 100/153 (65.4%) vs GW 139/153 (90.8%), GW better in 9/9 paired trials, 2 full passes (Vanguard). In-sample: graphs hand-built, mechanisms tuned on these tasks. Graph tools without the gate: no gain (Crestwood 16/22 x3).

profiles.name: B (typed rules from the policy build, write verifier)
profiles.why_not_best: nothing beat CUGA alone on IT service tasks, so this is a named profile for typed rules and not a measured best; do not read it as a result that won
profiles.result: no run beat CUGA alone on tasks passed: changes 26 (gpt-oss, tuning, 1 trial): verifiers 18/39 against 13/39 for CUGA alone, tasks passed 0/10 against 1/10; changes 38 (cross-reference tasks, brief only): verifiers 8/13 against 10/13
